extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and working creative writers; readers of Writer's Digest
extracted.subtask_description: A blog index page collecting short articles, essays, prompts, and resource links about creative-writing craft, voice, point of view, poetry forms, submission materials, and career advice aimed at writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Katauta form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The katauta is a Japanese poetic form that is actually considered an incomplete or half-poem. It’s a 3-liner that follows either 5-7-5 or more commonly 5-7-7 syllables per line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the katauta as a short, fragmentary form (a 'half-poem'); adhere to the syllabic pattern (5-7-5 or 5-7-7) when composing one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry prompt acceptance criteria (Reflection prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the reflection prompt: write a reflection poem—this could be about a physical reflection (or lack of reflection if you’re talking vampires). Poems that deal with reflections as thoughts work too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any creative interpretation of 'reflection' or reflective surfaces is acceptable; writers are invited to re-create and revise their poetry ('Re-create Your Poetry! Revision...'), indicating openness to varied approaches and to revision as part of the prompt practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make time for writing (career/time-management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make time for writing, because promotion can and will take over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical career advice: prioritize dedicated writing time, especially around book launches and promotion periods when non-writing demands increase; plan your schedule to protect creative time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty when writing villains in memoir
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing villains in memoir takes a special kind of honesty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying antagonistic figures in memoir, practice heightened honesty and ethical self-examination; be aware of the moral and factual responsibilities inherent in memoir writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission materials should hook agents/editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents will show you how to put together the best query letter, opening pages, and synopsis to hook the attention of Agents and Editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Queries, opening pages, and synopses should be crafted specifically to 'hook' industry readers—focus on clarity, compelling opening, and concise presentation of stakes and voice to capture agent/editor interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose POV appropriate to story and genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing which POV (point of view) to write in can be challenging. Writing instructor Pooja Mittal Biswas shares her suggestions for choosing the best POV for your story and genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select first- or third-person POV based on what best serves the story and fits genre expectations; consider which voice gives the necessary intimacy, scope, and reliability for your narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forced-proximity plausibility in romance
rubrics_metrics.description: Add believability to your romance story ideas with 50 legitimate reasons for them to be stuck together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using 'forced proximity' as a plot device, choose plausible, varied, and character-driven reasons for characters to be stuck together to increase credibility and emotional payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use structure to reinforce story
rubrics_metrics.description: Using structure to reinforce story: advice on how to choose the best story structure for your novels, with examples from award-winning books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a narrative structure intentionally so it amplifies theme, character arc, and pacing—use examples and structural techniques that align with the story’s emotional logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find and develop your writing voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding your writing voice: personal essays and exercises that helped an author discover his own voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work through exercises and sustained practice to develop a distinctive voice; voice emerges from choices in diction, rhythm, point of view, and attitude toward subject and reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use evidence-backed methods to beat writer’s block
rubrics_metrics.description: 10 Scientifically Proven Ways to Beat Writer’s Block — tips supported by scientific studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply empirically supported techniques (as summarized in the article) to overcome blocks; prefer strategies with research backing rather than solely anecdotal approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple POVs: clarity and reader satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice offering 5 tips for making writing in multiple points of view easier for you and more satisfying for your readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When employing multiple POVs, follow practical tips (e.g., distinct voice for each POV, clear transitions, consistent signaling) to maintain clarity and reader engagement.
